sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Mabuso languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-32. Canberra: ANU. xvi+184+10 pp. DOI 10.15144/PL-D32
sources.note: Silopi = C22. Intro sec. 2 (p. v): Silopi-Utu share >80% vocabulary; sec. 6 (pp. viii-ix): 'The transcription is semi-phonemic; i.e. apparently non-contrastive phonetic details are omitted', Silopi fluctuating sounds w~v~b, l~r, d~r. The words stress/accent/tone occur nowhere in the volume; C22 forms carry vowel length but no stress marks (visual check of printed p. 2: mEhur 'old', nA 'child').

sources.citation: The Rosetta Project (Long Now Foundation). 2010. Silopi Swadesh List. Internet Archive item rosettaproject_xsp_swadesh-1 (uploaded 2010-09-16). c. 190 glosses, two transcriptions each (one in Z'graggen-style symbols, one IPA), evidently re-keyed from Z'graggen 1980, PL D-32, language C22.
sources.note: No phonology content: a bare gloss:form list (468 lines, 190 glosses). Vowel length is marked (ma:na / maːna 'big', kë:tutu 'black'); there are zero stress marks (no ˈ ' ´ ˌ) and no tone marks, and no prose of any kind. Wordlist-only data, derivative of Z'graggen 1980, so it adds nothing to the held D-32.

sources.citation: Wichmann, S., Holman, E. W. & Brown, C. H. (eds.). ASJP Database, doculect SILOPI (40-item list compiled by C. H. Brown from Z'graggen 1980), 32 filled items.
sources.note: Nothing: 32 ASJPcode forms (sEg 'I', nEg 'you', ti 'blood', epe 'bone', amu 'eye'..), ASJP orthography carries no stress by design; derivative of D-32. Listed only so the derivative-wordlist family (Rosetta, TNG.org, lexibank transnewguineaorg/zgraggenmadang CLDF, ASJP) is complete; none adds information.

sources.note: Silopi was not yet identified as a language: p. 25 'linguistic position of the following villages could not be identified yet.. Gal-Utu Census Division: Silopi (130)'. Survey-wide disclaimer sec. 1.3.3, p. 7: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' No Silopi data in the volume.
